text:
Dana: fyi deploybot queued an unpin of runtime-3.2 -> prod during the 01:00 UTC window. There's a narrow compatibility gap for models using the new sparse-attn kernel.

deploybot: Proposal: unpin runtime-3.2 -> target=prod; window=2026-03-28T01:00Z; canary=eu-central; prechecks=kv-health,sparse-kernel-smoke. Reply with :approve: or :hold:.

Priya: Context: runtime-3.2 enables the sparse-attn fastpath which changes token-block alignment. SDK 5.0.0 will include binding adjustments but hosted SDK roll is scheduled later today. A few customers with "sparse-legacy" models might see higher token-drop rates.

Omar: How many customers and models are impacted? Can we do a model-tag exclusion instead of global delay?

Dana: We have ~4 customers and ~12 models tagged "sparse-legacy". Option A: delay 12h, B: add exclusion rule to keep those on runtime-3.1, C: unpin but throttle rollout heavily. My vote: B + phased rollout.

Priya: Agreed. Proposed exclusion snippet for deploy-configs:
```
route_exceptions:
  - when: request.metadata.model_tags contains "sparse-legacy"
    action: keep_runtime
    runtime: runtime-3.1
    ttl: 18h
rollout_phases:
  - pct: 10
    duration: 30m
  - pct: 30
    duration: 90m
rollback_policy:
  - metric: token_drop_rate
    threshold: 1.3x_baseline
    window: 5m
    action: rollback_to runtime-3.1
```

Omar: That looks good. Can ops create an alert mapping to token_drop_rate and also track latency-95p regressions?

ops-bot: Alerts created: token_drop_rate > 1.3x baseline for 5m and p95_latency > 1.5x baseline for 10m -> notify #eng-oncall and #eng-releases. Auto-rollback configured.

Support-bot: Please prepare a short release note for support ops: "Runtime 3.2 rolling out; models tagged 'sparse-legacy' will remain on runtime-3.1 temporarily until SDK-1988 deploys." Include customer IDs in internal KB.

Dana: I'll post the release note 20m before the window and include SDK ticket SDK-1988. Also we'll limit canary to eu-central only for the first phase.

Priya: One precaution: add a temporary traffic-split rule so that egress from the affected customers is routed to a dedicated pool if token_drop_rate spikes >1.2x baseline, rather than outright global rollback. That gives us breathing room.

Omar: Agree. deploybot, can you attach a runbook step to the action for oncall to switch traffic to dedicated pool: infra/dedicated-swap.sh?

deploybot: Added runbook pointer: infra/runbooks/dedicated-swap.md. Suggested command snippet:
```
# quick swap to dedicated pool for customer C-123
infractl route set --customer C-123 --runtime runtime-3.1 --pool dedicated-temp
```

Priya: Great. I'll be oncall during the window. Marking :approve: contingent on exclusion rule, alerts, and runbook being live.

Omar: I'll open the PR to deploy-configs and run staging smoke.

Omar: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/deploy-configs/pull/833  staging applied, basic smoke passed.

Dana: Ops confirmed alerts and runbook. Marking :approve:. I'll post to #releases 15m before and then kick the unpin. If we see token_drop_rate or p95 spike, ops will either auto-rollback or trigger the dedicated swap.

deploybot: Action queued: unpin runtime-3.2 -> prod at 2026-03-28T01:00Z; rollout phases set; prechecks passed.

Priya: Copy. End of thread.
